chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: E. Simms Campbell and Mrs. Anne Malone
summary: Thomas recalls cartoonist E. Simms Campbell, a telegraph boy, and Mrs. Anne Malone, who ran a scholarship fund for Black students.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: E. Simms Campbell. I thought he was tremendous.
And there was a lady by the name of Mrs. Malone, Mrs. Anne Malone. She had been old college (sounds like) at that time to take up the slack when kids couldn't go to school in Jeff City,

I mean to Missouri University, she had this little scholarship fund to send them to Illinois University. See what I mean? So Sims Campbell and me used to go to school up there ... (something about my own band). So Mrs. Malone -- I think she's a tremendous person -- she'd come up to Webster Groves and sit and talk to the kids, you know. Well, Sims I met around that time.
